newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to fine-tune natural monopolies' prices.
newsitem.headline: Russia to fine-tune natural monopolies' prices.

text.p: The Russian government plans to improve the system of natural monopolies prices regulation now that inflation has slowed down, Deputy Economy Minister Sergei Vasilyev said on Thursday.
During high inflation the government marked up prices charged by railways, electricity and gas producers, but now the inflation rate is falling this is too primitive, he said.
"1997 will be the year of transfer to a new price-making policy," Vasilyev told a news conference.
In March the government will work out a scheme which will relieve railways of social burdens, which account for 70 percent of their expenses against 30 percent in Europe, he said.
Prices for passanger transport, which accounts for 50 percent of all transport turnover, will be raised, he said.
Currently freight prices are 20 percent higher than passenger ones, with freight charges subsidising passenger costs, he said.
However the government planned to subsidise partially long-distance passenger transport, he said.

Prices and wages in the natural monopolies -- railways, gas producer RAO Gazprom and national power grid Unified Energy Systems (UES), have grown faster than in other industries, depriving them of financial means, Vasilyev said.
The government also plans to raise electricity and gas prices for households and cut them for companies, he said.
Draft regulations for this have already been drawn up, Vasilyev said.
On January 9 the government issued a law giving tax privileges to investment spending by UES until 2000, he said.
The law was passed without agreement from the Finance or Economy Ministers and his ministry was trying to persuade the government the privileges should be cancelled gradually, he said.
Vasilyev said changes in price policy were a key element in structural reform of the monopolies, something sought by the International Monetary Fund.
"There will be no restructuring before we get a normal tariff structure," he said.
